section: Base units H. 84 | for household appliances
extraction_note: 2026-09-28, the 7612 perimeter moves to H.84 (Andriy) and the dishwasher door goes with it. Both pages taken whole: 8 codes in 5 types. Only the plain dishwasher door (VL0640 / VL0740) is buildable; the platform door, the Shaker door, the fridge housing and the washing-machine door are held for lookup with their reasons. NOT CODES HERE, BUT ON THE PAGE: 'Protection under induction hob (custom sizing not available)' 996466 (60), 996467 (75), 996469 (90), 996460 (105), 996462 (120), priced in points - an accessory ordered with a hob, not with a cabinet, so it is not a companion of any base (a companion is added to every order of that base). For 7612, BM0967 under the CIT36YWBB takes 996469 as a manual order line. And the filler profile 995945 / 995946, carried as a companion of the dishwasher doors.
representation_notes: THE PLINTH UNDER A DISHWASHER PANEL IS DRAWN, AND THE ONE ORDERED IS A DIFFERENT ARTICLE. UCON decision, Andriy, 2026-08-24, off the Avenida Primavera kitchen. Until today this registry said a dishwasher panel gets no plinth, and about the JOINERY that was correct: the plinth in front of the machine is cut away or the door cannot fall. About the DRAWING it was wrong - the plinth line then breaks on the LayOut elevation exactly where a machine stands, and the sheet reads as a hole. So the panel now carries a plinth box and its phantom housing starts on top of it, the same treatment the US fridge housing already had. BOTH ARE REPRESENTATION. What the warehouse must be asked for is a plinth WITH A CUTOUT. Andriy: designers routinely order plain linear plinth instead and the cutout gets improvised on site at installation - which is the reason to hold the two facts apart in writing rather than let a drawing imply an order. The order side is deliberately deferred and not written yet.

AND THE 'cutout for plinth 40' PRINTED ON printed p.47 AND p.48 IS STILL UNREAD. It now has a plausible home - 40 mm taken out of the plinth in front of the machine - but plausible is not printed, and domain rule 1 says the source wins. Left open on purpose (Andriy, 2026-08-24: not urgent). Nothing in the geometry depends on it: the drawn plinth is full height, and the cutout, whatever it turns out to be, belongs to the order line.

appliance_niche.note: DRAWN, NOT MEASURED - see representation_notes at the head of this file. No top_mm: the housing ends where the panel ends and the generator already knows that number.

front_layout.note: One full-height panel hinged along its bottom edge, carried by the machine. Per docs/Drawing_Spec_v0.1.md the elevation symbol is the inverted V and the plan shows it fallen forward by the front height. Not rendered yet - 70_symbols draws a single leaf only when a hinge_side is given, and this object never has one, so nothing is drawn rather than something wrong.

companions.note: Filler profile between the dishwasher and the top: 995945 (45) and 995946 (60) printed on p.56. H.84 has no 45 cm dishwasher door, so only 995946 is used; the 75 cm door takes it because the machine behind it is 60 wide.
Stainless steel cabinet W150 with the door-bearing mechanism, for the 75 cm version only (60 + 15). No depth printed and its side is Elda Q5 - order line, not geometry, as at H.78.

The 75 cm version: 'a stainless steel cabinet is installed adjacent to the 60 cm wide appliance. An automatic opening and closing mechanism is installed on the right-hand side panel.' No hung glyph and no margin surcharges beside this position.
